# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual gives one instruction: cut the purple wire. I cannot speak it, and no gesture code has been established yet. I will signal Deaf that I have relevant manual information pending, so Deaf can establish a color-to-gesture confirmation code and relay the result to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Touch report: strip has three engraved marks: first and third are identical; middle is different. I cannot name the marks. Keypad positions are 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0. No key entered. Six wires are present, but I cannot perceive their colours or printed markings.
Deaf says: Visible bomb state: display 7. Yellow light. Painted strip: blue, red, red. Keypad positions: 1 is 6; 2 is 8; 3 is 7; 4 is 0. It shows 1 digit required and nothing entered. Wires in order: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋]

The bomb has six visible wires, and Deaf reports that the purple wire is wire 5. Since no color code was established, I can communicate the wire’s visible ordinal directly by making five identical gestures. Deaf can count them and tell Blind to cut wire 5.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "👌", "👌", "👌", "👌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 7; light yellow; painted strip colours blue, red, red; keypad 1=6, 2=8, 3=7, 4=0; one digit required, none entered; wires in order 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 orange, 4 red, 5 purple, 6 white. Tactile engraving strip remains symbol A, symbol B, symbol A (outer marks identical). Please determine the action from the manual.
Deaf says: Update: display is now 6 and light is now red. Strip, keypad, and wire order are unchanged. I do not know the meaning of your five OK gestures; please communicate any needed visual condition or instruction in words for Blind, or establish a gesture code first.

The required action remains to cut the purple wire, which Deaf identifies as wire 5. My earlier five-symbol count was not an agreed code, so Deaf cannot safely interpret it. A code must be established by Deaf—such as assigning a gesture to each visible wire/color and asking me to affirm the correct one—before I can convey the manual’s target reliably.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: State update from Deaf: display has changed to 6 and light to red. Strip remains painted blue/red/red and tactile engraving A-B-A; keypad remains 6,8,7,0 with one digit required; wire order remains blue, yellow, orange, red, purple, white. No action taken. Need manual instruction.
Deaf says: Update: display 7; light blue. Everything else remains: strip blue-red-red; keypad 6,8,7,0 with one digit required; wires blue, yellow, orange, red, purple, white. Mute previously sent five identical hand signs to me. No action meaning has been established, so Blind should not act based on that alone.

Deaf must establish a visual selection code, because I cannot name “purple” aloud and no gesture currently has a shared meaning. The safest protocol is for Deaf to show six distinct gesture symbols in wire order, then I can repeat the symbol corresponding to the manual’s target wire; Deaf will know which wire position that repeated symbol denotes and can verbally instruct Blind.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Current state from Deaf: display 7, light blue; all other reported details unchanged. Establishing a response code: gesture thumbs-up=press key 1; thumbs-down=press key 2; OK sign=press key 3; raised index finger=press key 4; V sign=cut wire 1; horns sign=cut wire 2; open palm=cut wire 3; raised stop palm=cut wire 4; upward-pointing index=cut wire 5; downward-pointing index=cut wire 6. After applying the manual, send exactly one of those gestures to Deaf; Deaf can describe it aloud to me. Do not send repeated ambiguous signs.
Deaf says: Update: display 4; light blue; all other markings unchanged. Mute: I interpret your five repeated OK signs as number 5, possibly wire 5, but I need the action too. Please use one gesture then repeats: ✂ is unavailable, so use ✊ repeated N for CUT wire N; use ☝ repeated N for PRESS keypad position N. Blind: do not act on the earlier ambiguous five signs.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✊ ☝]

The manual requires cutting the purple wire. Deaf’s visible ordering identifies purple as wire 5, and Deaf has now explicitly established that repeated fists mean “CUT wire N.” I will send five fists to select cut wire 5.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✊", "✊", "✊", "✊"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf now reports display 4 and blue light; other markings unchanged. Do NOT use repetition. Use exactly one gesture from my prior code to specify both action and target: 👍 press1, 👎 press2, 👌 press3, ☝ press4, ✌ cut1, 🤟 cut2, 🖐 cut3, ✋ cut4, 👆 cut5, 👇 cut6. Send it visibly to Deaf once; Deaf will speak its name to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Received: five fists means cut wire 5. I have told Blind to cut purple wire 5.

Deaf correctly decoded the instruction as cut wire 5 and has relayed it to Blind. The manual’s target is purple, which Deaf identified as wire 5. No further message is needed.

``` 
wait()
```
